text: Seventy-five K is enough? The data disagrees.
Heard it? Money stops buying happiness at seventy-five K.
That came from a 2010 study of over four hundred fifty thousand survey answers.
But another researcher pinged thirty-three thousand people on their phones.
Happiness kept rising, even past two hundred thousand.
The plateau was real. But only for the unhappiest fifteen to twenty percent.
For most people, happiness kept climbing.
The catch? It's small. About five points out of a hundred.
So money helps. Just less than you'd think.
